narrative.summary: The EU has adopted the world's first comprehensive AI law, the Artificial Intelligence Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), amended in 2026 by the Digital Omnibus on AI, together with implementing acts, Commission guidelines and voluntary codes of practice for general-purpose AI and AI-generated content. Earlier EU strategies (2018 Coordinated Plan, 2020 White Paper, 2025 AI Continent Action Plan and Apply AI Strategy) steer investment and adoption, while the Product Liability and Platform Work Directives add AI-relevant liability and algorithmic-management rules. The European Parliament, data protection authorities and EU agencies have issued resolutions, opinions and sector guidance on AI.

instruments.official_title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 June 2024 laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence (Artificial Intelligence Act)
instruments.english_title: Artificial Intelligence Act — Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
instruments.current_status: Entered into force on 1 August 2024. Prohibitions and AI-literacy duties apply from 2 February 2025, governance and general-purpose AI model rules from 2 August 2025 and most other rules from 2 August 2026; as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, high-risk rules apply from 2 December 2027 (Annex III) and 2 August 2028 (Annex I).
instruments.scope: European Union; personal and territorial scope governed by Article 2
instruments.summary: Risk-based rules for AI systems and general-purpose models. Application follows the Act’s timetable and amendments.

instruments.official_title: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 8 July 2026 amending Regulations (EU) 2024/1689, (EU) 2018/1139 and (EU) 2023/1230 as regards the simplification of the implementation of harmonised rules on artificial intelligence (Digital Omnibus on AI)
instruments.english_title: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 — Digital Omnibus on AI
instruments.current_status: Adopted 8 July 2026 and published in the Official Journal (L series 2026/1744) on 24 July 2026; the Commission states it entered into force on 27 July 2026.
instruments.summary: Amends the AI Act: moves the application of high-risk rules to 2 December 2027 (Annex III uses) and 2 August 2028 (AI in products under Annex I); softens the AI-literacy duty; adds simplified documentation and quality management for SMEs and small mid-caps; creates a legal basis for processing special-category data for bias detection; adds prohibitions on AI generating non-consensual intimate images and child sexual abuse material; and strengthens AI Office supervision of AI systems built on general-purpose models.

instruments.official_title: Commission Decision of 24 January 2024 establishing the European Artificial Intelligence Office (C/2024/1459)
instruments.english_title: Commission Decision establishing the European Artificial Intelligence Office
instruments.summary: Establishes the European AI Office within the Commission and sets its tasks: implementing and enforcing the AI Act, in particular for general-purpose AI models (evaluation tools, monitoring, investigation of infringements), preparing guidance, standards and codes of practice, acting as secretariat of the AI Board, cooperating with stakeholders and other EU bodies, and representing the Commission in international AI cooperation.
instruments.current_status: Adopted 24 January 2024 and published in the Official Journal (C series, C/2024/1459) on 14 February 2024; Article 9 states it entered into force on 21 February 2024.
instruments.evidence_reference: Read OJ C/2024/1459 header '14.2.2024', title and Art. 9 'shall enter into force on 21 February 2024' via eur-lex TXT/HTML. Commission decision binding on the Commission's own organisation (internal organisational act); classified binding_regulation as an EU decision.

instruments.official_title: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/454 of 7 March 2025 laying down the rules for the application of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards the establishment of a scientific panel of independent experts in the field of artificial intelligence
instruments.english_title: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/454 on the scientific panel of independent experts in AI
instruments.summary: Implements Article 68 of the AI Act by setting up the scientific panel of independent AI experts: selection and number of experts, independence and conflict-of-interest rules, the panel's tasks in supporting the AI Office (including qualified alerts on systemic risks of general-purpose AI models), and access by Member States to the experts.
instruments.current_status: Adopted 7 March 2025 and published in the Official Journal (L series 2025/454) on 10 March 2025; under Article 20 it entered into force on the twentieth day after publication.
instruments.evidence_reference: EUR-Lex ELI page read: date of act 7 March 2025, 'OJ L, 2025/454, 10.3.2025', Art. 20 twentieth-day entry into force (no calendar date printed, so effective_date left null).

instruments.official_title: Council Regulation (EU) 2024/1732 of 17 June 2024 amending Regulation (EU) 2021/1173 as regards a EuroHPC initiative for start-ups in order to boost European leadership in trustworthy artificial intelligence
instruments.english_title: Council Regulation (EU) 2024/1732 on a EuroHPC initiative for start-ups to boost European leadership in trustworthy AI (AI Factories)
instruments.summary: Amends the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking Regulation to add an AI Factories pillar: defines AI-optimised supercomputers and AI factories, lets the Joint Undertaking acquire and operate AI-optimised supercomputers (Union funding up to 50%), upgrade existing machines for AI, and give dedicated access to start-ups and SMEs for developing trustworthy general-purpose AI models in line with Union values.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the Council on 17 June 2024 and published in the Official Journal (L series 2024/1732) on 19 June 2024; it entered into force on 9 July 2024.
instruments.evidence_reference: OJ header 'L 2024/1732, 19.6.2024' and Art. 2 twentieth-day rule read via eur-lex TXT/HTML; EUR-Lex ELI page metadata prints first entry into force 9 July 2024.

instruments.official_title: Council Decision (EU) 2024/2218 of 28 August 2024 on the signing, on behalf of the European Union, of the Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law
instruments.english_title: Council Decision (EU) 2024/2218 on the signing, on behalf of the EU, of the Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI
instruments.summary: Authorises the signing of the Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law on behalf of the EU, subject to its later conclusion. The recitals state that the Union alone should become a party because of its exclusive external competence, and that the Convention will be implemented in the EU mainly through the AI Act.
instruments.current_status: Adopted 28 August 2024 and published in the Official Journal (L series 2024/2218) on 4 September 2024; Article 3 states it entered into force on the date of its adoption.
instruments.evidence_reference: ELI page read: 'OJ L, 2024/2218, 4.9.2024'; Art. 3 'shall enter into force on the date of its adoption' (28 August 2024). Council Decision on conclusion of the Convention not located (search budget exhausted).

instruments.official_title: Directive (EU) 2024/2831 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 October 2024 on improving working conditions in platform work
instruments.english_title: Platform Work Directive — Directive (EU) 2024/2831
instruments.summary: Sets EU rules for work through digital labour platforms. Chapter III on algorithmic management limits the processing of personal data by automated monitoring and decision-making systems, requires data-protection impact assessments, transparency to workers about these systems, human oversight, human review of significant decisions, health and safety safeguards, and information and consultation of workers' representatives.
instruments.current_status: Published in the Official Journal (L series 2024/2831) on 11 November 2024 and in force since 1 December 2024. Member States must transpose it by 2 December 2026.
instruments.evidence_reference: OJ header 'L 2024/2831, 11.11.2024'; Arts 7-15 titles; Art. 29(1) transposition 2 December 2026; Art. 31 twentieth day. EUR-Lex ELI metadata prints entry into force 1 December 2024.

instruments.official_title: Directive (EU) 2024/2853 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 October 2024 on liability for defective products and repealing Council Directive 85/374/EEC
instruments.english_title: Product Liability Directive — Directive (EU) 2024/2853
instruments.summary: Replaces the 1985 Product Liability Directive with no-fault liability rules for defective products that expressly include software, so AI systems are covered and their providers are treated as manufacturers. It addresses defects arising from updates and continuous learning of AI systems and eases the burden of proof where technical complexity, such as explaining how an AI system works, makes proof excessively difficult.
instruments.current_status: Published in the Official Journal (L series 2024/2853) on 18 November 2024 and in force since 8 December 2024. It applies to products placed on the market or put into service after 9 December 2026, the transposition deadline, when Directive 85/374/EEC is repealed.
instruments.evidence_reference: OJ header 'L 2024/2853, 18.11.2024'; Art. 4(1) product includes software; recitals 13, 40, 48 on AI systems; Art. 2(1), 21, 22(1) date 9 December 2026; EUR-Lex metadata entry into force 8 December 2024.

instruments.official_title: Commission Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence practices established by Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act)
instruments.english_title: Commission Guidelines on prohibited AI practices under the AI Act
instruments.summary: Explains the Commission's interpretation of the AI practices banned by Article 5 of the AI Act, including harmful manipulation and exploitation of vulnerabilities, social scoring, individual crime-risk prediction, untargeted facial-image scraping, emotion recognition at work and in education, biometric categorisation and real-time remote biometric identification for law enforcement, with practical examples for providers, deployers and authorities.
instruments.current_status: Published by the Commission on 4 February 2025 (page last updated 31 July 2025), together with the approval of the content of the draft Commission Communication on the guidelines. The Commission states the guidelines are non-binding and that authoritative interpretation is reserved to the Court of Justice of the EU.

instruments.english_title: Commission Guidelines on the AI system definition under the AI Act

instruments.english_title: Commission Guidelines on the scope of obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models
instruments.summary: Sets out the Commission's interpretation of who counts as a provider of a general-purpose AI model, when a model is general-purpose or poses systemic risk, how modifications and open-source exemptions work, and how the AI Office will supervise and enforce the obligations that applied from 2 August 2025.
instruments.current_status: Published by the Commission on 18 July 2025 with a Communication approving their content; available in all 24 official EU languages; non-binding.

instruments.english_title: Explanatory Notice and Template for the Public Summary of Training Content for general-purpose AI models
instruments.summary: Provides the template, required by Article 53(1)(d) of the AI Act, that providers of general-purpose AI models use to publish a sufficiently detailed summary of the content used to train their models, with an explanatory notice setting a common minimum baseline on data sources, data processing and copyright-relevant information.
instruments.current_status: Published by the Commission on 24 July 2025 in all official EU languages, with an editable English template.

instruments.summary: Draft guidelines under Article 6(5) of the AI Act explaining how to decide whether an AI system is high-risk, either as a safety component of a product under Annex I legislation or through an Annex III use case, with practical examples of systems that are and are not high-risk.

instruments.official_title: Draft Guidance Article 73 AI Act – Incident Reporting, and Incident report template for serious incidents under the AI Act (high-risk AI systems)
instruments.english_title: Draft guidance and reporting template on serious AI incidents (Article 73 AI Act)
instruments.summary: Draft guidance explaining when and how providers of high-risk AI systems must report serious incidents to market surveillance authorities under Article 73 of the AI Act, with a draft reporting template.

instruments.official_title: Commission opinion on the assessment of the Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-generated Content
instruments.english_title: Commission opinion on the assessment of the Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-generated Content
instruments.issuing_authority: European Commission (with AI Board adequacy assessment)
instruments.publisher_name: European Commission (with AI Board adequacy assessment)
instruments.summary: The Commission's assessment that the Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-generated Content adequately covers the AI Act's transparency obligations in Article 50(2), (4) and (5), accompanied by the AI Board's adequacy assessment. It invites generative AI providers and deployers to sign and notes that adherence is not conclusive proof of compliance.

instruments.official_title: Artificial Intelligence for Europe (COM(2018) 237 final)
instruments.english_title: Artificial Intelligence for Europe
instruments.summary: Commission Communication setting out a European approach to AI: boosting the EU's technological and industrial capacity and AI uptake, preparing for socio-economic changes in education, training and the labour market, and ensuring an appropriate ethical and legal framework based on Union values. It calls for AI investment of at least EUR 20 billion by the end of 2020 and more than EUR 20 billion per year in the following decade.
instruments.current_status: Commission Communication COM(2018) 237 final, dated Brussels, 25 April 2018; it announced a coordinated plan with Member States by the end of 2018.
instruments.evidence_reference: EUR-Lex text: 'Brussels, 25.4.2018 COM(2018) 237 final'. | Independent check 2026-10-21: 'later built on by the Coordinated Plans on AI and the AI Act' is not in the source (it only announces a coordinated plan by end-2018); summary's 'first AI strategy' not stated in the source

instruments.official_title: Coordinated Plan on Artificial Intelligence (COM(2018) 795 final)
instruments.english_title: Coordinated Plan on Artificial Intelligence (2018)
instruments.summary: Joint plan of the Commission, Member States, Norway and Switzerland to pool investment, data, skills and research on AI, with the annexed 'Coordinated Plan on the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence Made in Europe – 2018' and an aim of EUR 20 billion a year in public and private AI investment over the next decade; it encouraged every Member State to adopt a national AI strategy.
instruments.current_status: Commission Communication COM(2018) 795 final of 7 December 2018, prepared with Member States, Norway and Switzerland. Draft Council conclusions welcoming it were forwarded for adoption on 18 February 2019, and the plan was revised by the Coordinated Plan on AI 2021 Review.

instruments.english_title: Building Trust in Human-Centric Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: Commission Communication endorsing the seven key requirements for trustworthy AI drawn from the High-Level Expert Group's ethics guidelines, launching a piloting phase for the assessment list and setting out work to build international consensus on human-centric AI.

instruments.english_title: Fostering a European approach to Artificial Intelligence, including the Coordinated Plan on AI 2021 Review
instruments.summary: Communication accompanying the AI Act proposal, with the Coordinated Plan on AI 2021 Review agreed with Member States: sets joint actions to create enabling conditions for AI (data, compute, governance), build excellence from lab to market, ensure AI works for people, and build strategic leadership in high-impact sectors such as health, climate, public sector, mobility and agriculture.

instruments.official_title: Communication on boosting startups and innovation in trustworthy artificial intelligence (COM(2024) 28 final)
instruments.english_title: Communication on boosting startups and innovation in trustworthy artificial intelligence
instruments.summary: Sets out a strategic investment framework for trustworthy AI, including AI Factories built around EuroHPC supercomputers, faster common European data spaces, the GenAI4EU initiative to develop generative AI applications in industrial and public sectors, and financing for AI start-ups and scale-ups.
instruments.current_status: Commission Communication of 24 January 2024, part of the AI innovation package.
instruments.evidence_reference: EUR-Lex text: 'Brussels, 24.1.2024 COM(2024) 28 final'.

instruments.official_title: AI Continent Action Plan (COM(2025) 165 final)
instruments.english_title: AI Continent Action Plan
instruments.summary: Aims to make the EU a leading AI continent by scaling computing infrastructure (AI Factories and AI Gigafactories), improving access to high-quality data, accelerating AI adoption in strategic sectors, strengthening AI skills and talent, and simplifying AI Act implementation, notably for smaller companies, including through an AI Act Service Desk.

instruments.evidence_reference: EUR-Lex text: 'Brussels, 9.4.2025 COM(2025) 165 final'.

instruments.official_title: Ethics guidelines for trustworthy AI

instruments.issuing_authority: High-Level Expert Group on Artificial Intelligence (set up by the European Commission)
instruments.publisher_name: High-Level Expert Group on Artificial Intelligence (set up by the European Commission)
instruments.summary: Defines trustworthy AI as lawful, ethical and robust and sets seven key requirements: human agency and oversight; technical robustness and safety; privacy and data governance; transparency; diversity, non-discrimination and fairness; societal and environmental well-being; and accountability.
instruments.current_status: Presented by the High-Level Expert Group on AI on 8 April 2019, after a first draft published in December 2018 drew more than 500 comments in an open consultation. The Commission's Communication COM(2019) 168 of the same day supports its seven key requirements and notes the guidelines are non-binding.
instruments.evidence_reference: Commission library page dated 8 April 2019. Issued by Commission expert group, published by Commission. | Independent check 2026-10-21: source page does not mention the Commission Communication or call the guidelines voluntary (COM(2019) 168 does note they are non-binding and that the Commission 'supports' the seven requirements)

instruments.publisher_name: High-Level Expert Group on Artificial Intelligence (set up by the European Commission)
instruments.summary: The High-Level Expert Group's second deliverable: recommendations to the Commission and Member States on policy and investment for trustworthy AI, covering human-centric use, the public sector, research, skills, data and infrastructure, and governance and regulation.
instruments.current_status: Presented by the High-Level Expert Group on AI, an independent expert group set up by the Commission, on 26 June 2019 as its second deliverable after the Ethics Guidelines (page last updated 8 March 2021).

instruments.official_title: Presidency conclusions: The Charter of Fundamental Rights in the context of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Change
instruments.english_title: Presidency conclusions on the Charter of Fundamental Rights in the context of AI and digital change
instruments.issuing_authority: Presidency of the Council of the European Union
instruments.publisher_name: Presidency of the Council of the European Union
instruments.summary: Sets out how the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights should guide the design, development and use of AI: human-centric AI, conditions for limiting rights, human oversight, transparency, documentation and accountability, adequately resourced supervisors, and concerns about bias, opacity, mass surveillance and threats to elections and fair trials.

instruments.official_title: Council Regulation (EU) 2026/150 of 16 January 2026 amending Regulation (EU) 2021/1173 on establishing the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking
instruments.english_title: Council Regulation (EU) 2026/150 on AI Gigafactories (amending the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking Regulation)
instruments.summary: Amends the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking Regulation to add an 'AI gigafactory pillar'. It defines AI gigafactories as large-scale facilities covering the full lifecycle of very large AI models, and provides for their establishment to give researchers, industry, SMEs and the public sector access to AI computing, including for foundation models. The Union may fund up to 17% of the computing infrastructure's capital expenditure, matched by participating states; access time is proportional to contributions, free Union access is set for certain users, and access by third-country entities can be restricted on strategic or security grounds.
instruments.current_status: Council Regulation published in the Official Journal (OJ L, 2026/150, 19.1.2026); it entered into force on the day following publication (20 January 2026) and is binding in its entirety and directly applicable in the Member States.
instruments.evidence_reference: Read on EUR-Lex: title and date from the ELI page; OJ line 'OJ L, 2026/150, 19.1.2026' and Article 3 entry-into-force wording from the HTML text (uri=OJ:L_202600150); entry into force 20 January 2026 per EUR-Lex document information. Resolves first-pass could_not_verify item. 'Directly applicable' is standard Regulation wording; verify the final article if needed.

instruments.official_title: European Parliament resolution of 10 March 2026 on copyright and generative artificial intelligence – opportunities and challenges (2025/2058(INI))
instruments.english_title: European Parliament resolution on copyright and generative artificial intelligence – opportunities and challenges
instruments.summary: Own-initiative resolution on copyright and generative AI. Parliament asks the Commission to examine fair remuneration for past uses of protected works by general-purpose AI providers, calls for itemised disclosure of copyright-protected material used for training and other uses, with a rebuttable presumption of use where transparency duties are not met, standardised machine-readable opt-outs from text and data mining possibly managed by the EUIPO, voluntary sector-based collective licensing, robust enforcement by the AI Office of the copyright chapter of the General-Purpose AI Code of Practice, and application of EU copyright rules to all generative AI models offered on the EU market.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the European Parliament on 10 March 2026 (P10_TA(2026)0066). A non-legislative resolution; it does not create legal obligations.
